description: SQLite schema for the local project management MVP with one board per authenticated user and room for future multi-user expansion.

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores the signed-in users supported by the MVP and future multi-user expansion.
notes: This table is intentionally minimal for the MVP.
The current app uses the hardcoded demo login, but the schema is ready for additional users later.

tables.name: boards
tables.purpose: Stores the board for each user. The MVP only allows one board per user.
notes: The UNIQUE constraint on user_id keeps the MVP to a single board per user without preventing future expansion to multiple boards per user.

tables.name: columns
tables.purpose: Defines the ordered set of board columns and their display titles.
notes: The current frontend has five fixed columns: Backlog, Discovery, In Progress, Review, and Done.
The position column preserves ordering between columns.

tables.name: cards
tables.purpose: Stores the cards inside each column, including card order and note content.
notes: Cards are tracked by column_id and position so drag-and-drop ordering is preserved without storing a separate movement log.
The details field replaces the current per-card metadata pattern used in the frontend demo.

relationship_summary.data_shape: Each board has a fixed ordered column list, and each card belongs to one column with a position value.

mvp_assumptions: The app will support a single board per user in the MVP.
Authentication is still a simple hardcoded sign-in flow for the demo, but user records exist in the database model for future expansion.
The board and all its columns/cards are stored in SQLite and recreated automatically if the database does not already exist.
Column names and card order are persisted in the database rather than only in browser memory.
